info.title: NESC exchange API
info.description: The Texstar exchange runner API of NESC (Phase 1b): signed NESC -> PMO packages out, PMO -> NESC packages in (single-shot or chunked with a client uuid), files by sha256, direct row pushes and the import ledger. Bearer tokens only (a field login / pairing token or an API client token); every POST / PUT needs an Idempotency-Key; every error is {"error": {"code", "message", "row"?, "correlation_id"?}}. PMO exposes the identical surface.

head.description: 200 with `Content-Length` and `X-Mime` when the sha256 is registered and its bytes exist; 404 otherwise.

get.description: The bytes as an attachment named `<sha256>.<ext>` with the stored finfo mime and `nosniff`.

put.description:
Raw body (the client `Content-Type` is ignored; the mime is sniffed and must be in the allowlist,
else 422 `unsupported_media`); the body must hash to `{sha256}` (400 `hash_mismatch`) and stay under
`max_file_mb` (413 `file_too_large`). 201 when stored, 200 when the sha was already registered.

get.description:
Imports with an internal id above `since` in ascending order (`limit` <= 200, default 50), optionally
filtered by `kind` (package | rows) or `status`; `next_since` continues the walk (null at the end).

The import document plus the rejected rows recorded at staging (`verdicts`, 100 per `page`, each
addressed by stream, seq and key).
get.summary: One import with its row verdicts

get.description:
Kind, producer package id, scope, direction, status, `rejected_code`, per-stream counts, the first
200 rejects (by stream, seq and key), warnings and the number of embedded receipts applied.
NESC's receipt for the package (applied, or rejected after the manifest verified); 404 until one exists.

post.description:
Multipart `package` (<= `limits.max_upload_mb`; larger packages go through chunks) and optional
`auto_apply`. 202 with the import to poll; the same bytes already received are answered 200 with
that import; a `rejected|failed` import of the same bytes is re-staged in place for its owner
(202) and refused to anyone else (409 `conflict`).
post.summary: Upload a package in one body

post.description:
Owner only. Assembles the chunks in order, compares the sha256 with `sha256` (400 `hash_mismatch`
when they differ; the chunks stay for a retry), stores the package and stages it off the request
(202). 404 for an unknown uuid.

Owner only; 409 unless the import is `previewed`. `allow_large_drop` lets a full poles set past the
drop guard. Runs off the request (202); the apply is claimed atomically, so a second request for
the same import applies nothing.

`{uuid}` is a client-generated v4 uuid. The first chunk creates the `uploading` import owned by the
caller (409 `conflict` when the uuid exists under another principal); `chunk_index` / `total_chunks`
(<= max_chunks) / `checksum` (sha256 of the chunk body). The same (index, checksum) again is
idempotent; the same index under another checksum is 409; a running total over `max_package_mb`
is 413 `package_too_large` and fails the import. A principal may hold at most three unfinished
uploads (409 `too_many_uploads`); an upload idle for 24 hours is removed by exchange:prune.

get.description:
`application/x-ndjson`, one row per line from `cursor` (a 0-based seq) up to `limit` (<= 1000)
rows; `X-Next-Cursor`, `X-Has-More` and `X-Stream-Schema` headers. 409 until the package is ready.
get.summary: Page one stream of an outbound package

post.description:
Queues a build of every outbox row PMO has not receipted (202, poll `status_url`). A `ready`
unreceipted package whose pending set is unchanged is answered 200 instead of rebuilt. 503
`signing_not_configured` when NESC holds no HMAC secret for its key id.

get.description: The signed `*.txx.zip` as an attachment with `X-Package-Sha256`; 409 until the package is ready.

post.description:
`{rows: [...]}` (JSON) or one row per line as `application/x-ndjson`, at most 500 rows; `dry_run=1`
previews without applying. The answer lists a verdict per row by `seq` and `key`
(applied | accepted | rejected | refused). Delta streams only: a full-mode stream (poles,
packets_wanted, gis_sources, gis_features, pge_violations) replaces the whole set, so it is 422
`full_stream_requires_package` and travels only in a signed package.

get.description:
The transport in force, the contract version and stream catalogue, the scope, whether outbound
signing is configured, the size limits a runner must respect (`limits`: max_upload_mb for one
body, max_package_mb for an assembled upload, chunk_mb, max_file_mb), the last package in each
direction, staleness, pending outbox rows per stream, cursors and the last external_refs drift check.

last_outbound.description: Scalars are cast so the OpenAPI document (Scramble) does not depend on the generating database's schema.

post.description:
JSON `{ops: [UpdateOp...], dry_run?, create?}` (at most 2000 ops) or multipart `workbook` (.xlsx from
GET /updates/workbook, edited) with `dry_run` / `create`. Up to 500 ops answer 200 with a verdict per
op (`applied | unchanged | rejected | forbidden | unknown_key | unsupported_until_1d`, addressed by
`seq`, `op_id` and `key`); more answer 202 with the batch to poll at GET /imports/{id}. `dry_run`
previews through the same dispatcher and writes nothing; `create` (unknown keys become rows) is
Phase 1d's and is answered `unsupported_until_1d`.

get.description:
The .xlsx with sheets Jobs, Tasks, Poles, Violations and Holds: read-only columns grey, editable
columns white (blank = no change, CLEAR empties), Phase 1d columns yellow, a Lists legend, and hidden
`_meta` / `_base_*` sheets that let the import tell an edit from an exported value. `program` stamps
the scope.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
